signals.title: NOK/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NOK leads the G10 currency strength scorecard with a 1W average of +1.018% across 2 pairs, while JPY anchors the board as the prime laggard at -0.604% across 7 pairs. This generates an active 1.621% bilateral leader-to-laggard spread, exceeding the 1.20% threshold. Norges Bank policy rate of 4.5% vs BoJ at 1.25% provides a +325bp carry advantage favoring NOK, reinforced by a +1.82% Norwegian real policy rate against Japan's deeply negative -2.25%. JPY remains vulnerable ahead of the Bank of Japan monetary policy statement, where a hold at 1.25% is expected alongside persistent downside pressure on Japanese yields. Trade bias: Long NOK/JPY; policy divergence and carry advantage favor continued outperformance. Catalyst: BoJ Interest Rate Decision at ~02:30 UTC. Risk: BoJ delivers a surprise hawkish dissent or guidance shift that sparks abrupt yen short-covering.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Technical Range
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.80, contained inside a tight 20-session box below its SMA20 at 157.91 and SMA200 at 158.48, with the 50-day average at 157.44 defining immediate support. FX options show 1M 25-delta risk reversals printing at -2.08, indicating an acute put skew and heavy institutional demand for downside protection despite spot holding near the top of its range. While Fed SOFR at 3.94% vs BoJ TONA at 1.23% secures a +271bp carry advantage favoring USD, VRP sits at +1.5% with 1M IV at 7.0% against HV30 of 5.5%. Speculative accounts trimmed shorts WoW by +12,222 contracts to net -25,598, aligning with heavy options hedging rather than fresh upside chasing into event risk. Trade bias: Neutral/short USD/JPY; pronounced put skew caps upside through the moving-average resistance band. Catalyst: BoJ Interest Rate Decision and Press Conference at ~02:30 UTC / 06:30 UTC. Risk: BoJ firmly commits to an extended pause, triggering a clean technical breakout above 158.50.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Divergence + Front-End Yield Support
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7029, testing its 50-day SMA at 0.7072 and steep 200-day SMA at 0.7058 after clearing short-term resistance above 0.7022 and holding above the SMA20 at 0.6992. Cash policy rates favor the Australian dollar, with RBA at 4.6% vs Fed at 4.0%, yielding a -60bp carry differential favoring AUD, while OIS pricing yields a -66bp carry advantage (SOFR 3.94% vs AONIA 4.60%). Front-end sovereign momentum reinforces the move as the AU-US 2Y yield spread has tightened +11bp over the last 5 sessions to +25bp. Following hot domestic inflation prints, institutional desks increasingly anticipate a back-to-back 25bp hike from the RBA next week, contrasting with an on-hold Federal Reserve. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; widening policy divergence and front-end yield support favor extension toward 0.7100. Catalyst: Australia Q/Q PPI release at 00:30 UTC ahead of the RBA meeting on 3 Nov. Risk: AU PPI misses forecast sharply and eases RBA hike pricing back toward a neutral hold.
evidence: Fed 4.0% vs RBA 4.6% — 60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Technical Downtrend
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1187, holding in an established downtrend below its falling SMA20 at 1.1206, SMA50 at 1.1402, and SMA200 at 1.1570. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds net short -94,138 contracts, situated at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.72, signaling acute institutional short positioning. Fed SOFR at 3.94% vs ECB €STR at 2.44% generates a +150bp carry differential favoring USD, keeping structural upside capped. Concurrently, retail traders hold an extreme 85% long exposure, creating an active contrarian headwind against institutional positions as German and Eurozone Q3 GDP prints approach. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; established technical downtrend and USD carry advantage dominate despite stretched institutional shorts. Catalyst: Euro Area Q3 Flash GDP release at 10:00 UTC. Risk: Eurozone growth data sharply exceeds expectations while ECB December hike pricing accelerates, triggering a short squeeze through the 1.1210 SMA20 hurdle.
evidence: Fed 4.0% vs ECB 2.65% — 135bp USD carry advantage
